title: #1 Einstein
prompt: “The only thing that interferes with my learning is education.” – Albert Einstein. What did he mean by that? Do you think he is correct?

variants.label: Version 1: AGREE
variants.essay:
Education is important for people's lives. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that school education can sometimes stop real learning. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One clear advantage is that school lessons can limit a person's real interests. School often teaches many facts, but it does not always teach how to think. For example, a student might love art, yet the school program focuses only on math. This means the student does not get time to learn about art in a deep way. Also, learning should come from what we are interested in, not just what we must study. This shows that personal interests are key to good learning.

Another reason is that school can make learning feel like a job. Students spend many hours in a classroom, and they must follow a set plan. This is because the focus is on passing tests, not on enjoying knowledge. For example, a child might learn history by reading dates, but they do not learn about the people who lived then. This limits their understanding of life. Also, real learning happens when we explore things outside of school. This suggests that practical experience is better than just book study.

I strongly agree that school education can sometimes stop real learning. We must focus on personal interests and also find ways to explore outside of school to improve our knowledge.

analysis.point1: School education often limits personal interests and deep understanding.
analysis.point2: The focus on testing and curriculum makes learning feel like a chore.

title: #2 Healthy Diet
prompt: A healthy diet is more effective for keeping fit than exercise. What is your opinion?

variants.label: Version 1: AGREE
variants.essay:
Many people think that keeping fit needs both good food and exercise. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that a healthy diet is more effective for keeping fit than exercise. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

First, good food gives the body the right energy it needs. This is because food provides the vitamins and nutrients that help our body work well. For example, eating enough fruits and vegetables gives us strong bodies and helps us feel good all day. This shows that proper eating is the main source of energy for our body. Also, good food helps us stay strong and keeps us healthy.

Second, a healthy diet helps us feel better when we do physical activity. This is because good food keeps our muscles strong and helps us feel better after moving. For example, if we eat good food, our muscles can repair themselves after running or walking. This means that good food makes exercise more helpful for our health. Another reason is that good food gives us the power to do more things.

I strongly agree that a healthy diet is more important for keeping fit than exercise. Good food gives the body the right energy, and it also helps us feel better when we do physical activity.

analysis.point1: The essay argues that diet is more important than exercise for fitness.
analysis.point2: It uses simple examples (fruits, protein) and simple connectors (First, Second, For example) to support the view.

The relative importance of dietary intake compared to physical activity for maintaining physical fitness is a subject of ongoing debate. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that a healthy diet is more important for keeping fit than exercise. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

A primary reason for prioritizing diet is that proper nutrition provides the fundamental building blocks for the body. This is because the nutrients we consume directly influence our metabolic rate and overall energy levels. For instance, consuming a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals ensures that our bodily functions operate optimally, preventing nutritional deficiencies. Consequently, even if one engages in rigorous exercise, inadequate dietary habits will undermine the body's ability to recover and function effectively. This emphasizes that diet is foundational to physical health.

Another compelling argument suggests that diet dictates the body's capacity to sustain physical activity. This is because the quality of food determines the sustained energy supply needed for prolonged physical conditioning. A practical example is an athlete who consumes processed foods; they will experience rapid energy spikes followed by severe crashes, limiting their performance. Maintaining optimal fitness requires a consistent intake of nutritious food to support sustained physical effort, which is crucial for peak performance.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that a healthy diet is more important for keeping fit than exercise. Proper nutrition provides the fundamental building blocks, and a consistent intake of nutritious food is essential for optimal fitness.

Advertisements can make people buy items they do not need, and they can also give people information. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that advertisements make people buy things they do not need or cannot afford. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, advertisements make people buy things they do not need. In other words, ads make people want things they do not really need in daily life. For example, ads for clothes show people that they need many new items. As a result, people spend money on things they do not need. This shows that ads can make people buy things they do not need.

For example, ads for health food show people about good ways to live. As a result, people learn about better ways to improve their life. This supports the view that ads can give people useful information.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with the view that advertisements make people buy things they do not need or cannot afford. This is clear from hand and other.

This clearly aligns with the view that advertising can foster excessive consumerism.

variants.label: Version 2: DISAGREE
variants.essay:
Some people believe that every city and town must include a large public open space for its residents. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with the view that every city should have at least one large public open space. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

While having open spaces is good, making it a requirement for every location is too much. In other words, these spaces must fit the needs and size of the local area. For instance, a small village does not need a huge park like a major city. As a result, forcing such a large space can waste valuable land that could be used for housing. Hence, it becomes evident that local needs should guide the size of public green areas.

Another reason is that forcing a large space is not always practical for all communities. This is primarily due to the fact that some areas have unique geographical challenges, such as steep hills or rivers. This can be exemplified by the fact that building a large, flat park in such terrain is very difficult and costly. The outcome is that the money spent on the park could be better used for improving other necessary facilities. This clearly aligns with the view that urban planning must consider practical limitations.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the view that every city should have at least one large public open space. This is clear from while and another.

variants.label: Version 2: DISAGREE
variants.essay:
The necessity of large public open spaces in all urban settlements is a subject of considerable debate. In my opinion, I strongly disagree with the view that every city should have at least one large public open space. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

While green areas are beneficial for community well-being, mandating a large public open space in every town is impractical. In other words, urban planning must consider diverse geographical and economic realities. For instance, densely populated industrial zones often lack the necessary acreage for a substantial park. As a result, forcing such a facility could necessitate the demolition of existing, functional residential structures. Hence, it becomes evident that alternative, smaller-scale green infrastructure solutions are more appropriate.

Furthermore, focusing solely on large parks overlooks the unique needs of specific local areas. This is primarily due to the fact that smaller, decentralized amenities better serve varied community needs. This can be exemplified by the fact that some neighborhoods thrive with a network of small community gardens and pocket parks. The outcome is that these distributed spaces enhance accessibility and foster localized community cohesion. This clearly aligns with the view that tailored, varied green spaces are superior to a single, massive facility.

In conclusion, I strongly disagree with the view that every city should have at least one large public open space. This is clear from while and furthermore.

title: #9 Global Issue
prompt: Climate change is a concerning global issue. Who has the main responsibility to take action to solve this problem, governments, large companies, or individuals?

variants.label: Version 1: GOVERNMENT
variants.essay:
Climate change is a big problem for our world today. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that governments have the main responsibility to take action on climate change. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Governments must take the main action to solve climate change. In other words, they can set rules for how people and companies must act in daily life in daily life. For example, a government can make rules to limit car pollution in big cities. As a result, the air quality will get much better for all people. This shows that governments are needed to make big changes.

Governments also have the main responsibility to help the planet. This is because they control the energy sources and the laws that guide them in daily life. For example, a government can give money to build wind power plants. As a result, people will use less dirty energy from burning oil. This supports the view that governments must lead the way.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that governments have the main responsibility to take action on climate change. Governments must set rules for pollution, and they must also lead the way in using clean energy.

Climate change represents a significant and complex global challenge that demands immediate and coordinated action. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that governments have the main responsibility to take action on climate change. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

Governments bear the primary responsibility for addressing climate change because they possess the necessary authority and resources to enact large-scale policy shifts. In other words, only state institutions can mandate sweeping changes across entire economies and sectors. For instance, a national government can implement carbon pricing mechanisms or mandate the phase-out of fossil fuels. As a result, industries are compelled to adopt cleaner technologies, accelerating the transition to a sustainable energy mix. Hence, it becomes evident that governmental policy is the most potent catalyst for global decarbonization.

Furthermore, governments are crucial because they are responsible for establishing the regulatory framework that guides corporate behavior. This is primarily due to the fact that without clear laws, large corporations may prioritize profit over ecological balance. This can be exemplified by the fact that national environmental protection agencies can enforce strict emission standards on manufacturing plants. The outcome is that businesses are incentivized to invest in research and development of low-carbon alternatives. This clearly aligns with the view that governmental oversight is essential for corporate accountability.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with the view that governments have the main responsibility to take action on climate change. This is clear from governments and furthermore.

title: #10 Communication
prompt: Communication has changed significantly in the last 10 years. Discuss the positive and negative impacts of this change.

variants.label: Version 1: MORE POSITIVE
variants.essay:
Communication methods have changed a lot in the last ten years. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that changes in communication have more positive impacts than negative impacts. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

On the one hand, one clear advantage is that people are more connected because of new technology. This is because we can talk to friends all over the world very fast. For example, social media lets us share photos and news. This makes keeping in touch with family easy and fun, which is a big help for people. variants.label: Version 1: DISCUSSION
variants.essay:
Students have several ways to get information about academic subjects, such as using books, online sources, or talking to teachers and friends. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that discussion with teachers and peers is the most reliable source of academic information. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One main reason why talking to teachers and peers is the best source is that people can ask questions and get immediate answers. When we discuss a subject with a teacher, they can explain difficult parts in a way that is easy to understand. For example, if a student reads something confusing in a book, the teacher can correct the misunderstanding right away. This direct discussion helps make sure the information is accurate and correct for the student.

Another important reason is that discussing subjects with peers helps students learn how to think critically and check facts. When friends talk about a topic, they share different views and ideas, which makes the information stronger. For instance, if two students discuss a history event, they might check the facts against what they read online, making the knowledge more solid. This process of talking together helps students understand the full picture and different sides of the issue.

I strongly agree that discussing subjects with teachers and peers is the most reliable source. This is because teachers provide clear explanations, and friends help students check facts and understand different views.

analysis.point1: Discussion with teachers provides immediate, expert clarification, ensuring accuracy.
analysis.point2: Discussion with peers promotes critical thinking and fact-checking through shared viewpoints.

variants.label: Version 2: PRINTED BOOKS
variants.essay:
Students have several ways to get information about academic subjects, such as using the internet, reading printed books, or talking with teachers and classmates. In my opinion, I strongly agree with the view that printed books and articles are the most reliable source of academic information. This essay will provide two reasons supporting my idea.

One clear advantage is that printed books and articles offer deep and structured knowledge. This is because these materials have gone through careful editing and checking by experts. For example, a textbook on history will present facts that have been reviewed by many scholars, making the information very reliable. This supports the view that printed books provide a solid foundation of verified knowledge.

Another reason is that printed books provide a stable and focused learning experience. This is because reading from a physical book helps students concentrate without the many distractions found online. A practical example is that when studying for an exam, a student can read the same chapter repeatedly, which helps them remember the details better. This shows that printed books help students learn in a focused way.

In conclusion, I strongly agree with the view that printed books and articles are the most reliable source of academic information. This is clear from clear and another.
